% (1) main-text paragraph (120 words, <= 120)
\textbf{Multivariate control.} On the 11 TF-motif tasks (9 exact-duplicate-free sequence sets) we regressed MCC on discriminability plus nine pre-registered covariates, including length, within-class GC SD and train/test homology. Selection-honest nested leave-one-task-out search did not beat discriminability alone (MAE 0.143 vs.\ 0.140; $\Delta$ 95\% CI $[-0.05,+0.07]$); the discriminability+length+GC-SD+homology model was worse (0.233). Homology did not confound discriminability (partial $\rho{=}+0.74$), but discriminability is collinear with GC content ($\rho{=}+0.69$); both separate the solved promoter from the failing enhancer/OCR tasks. Post hoc, GC alone tracks MCC at least as closely ($\rho{=}+0.86$; MAE 0.086); discriminability beats GC on the seven homology-clean tasks (0.039 vs.\ 0.123) only via the three-class regulatory task (without it: 0.040 vs.\ 0.034). Real tasks cannot isolate discriminability; the synthetic dose-response does.

% (2) rebuttal paragraph (response letter, R1.1; 380 words)
We fitted the requested regression on the real tasks (plan pre-registered; nine covariates incl. length, within-class GC SD and 8-mer train/test homology; all <=3-covariate subsets; selection-honest nested leave-one-task-out). At n=11 TF-motif tasks no covariate set improved on discriminability (MAE 0.143 vs 0.140, Delta CI [-0.05,+0.07], incremental permutation p=0.43). The discriminability + length + GC-SD + homology model you asked for overfits (LOTO MAE 0.233; with 6 residual df no coefficient's CI excludes 0; on all 15 tasks only discriminability's bootstrap CI excludes 0, while length's t-CI [-1.07,-0.03] excludes 0 but its bootstrap CI does not). Test-set sampling noise explains 1.5% of the misfit; the rest is between-task heterogeneity. Post hoc, its main axis is that the real MCCs form two non-overlapping clusters, the solved promoter/regulatory and the failing enhancer/OCR tasks of Table I, which discriminability and GC content (rho +0.69) both separate. GC content tracks MCC at least as closely as discriminability (rho +0.86 vs +0.74; difference CI [-0.32,+0.53]) and predicts held-out MCC at least as well (within 0.005 MCC) on all 11 tasks (MAE 0.086, a model chosen in-sample) and on every other task set we examined, except the Genomic-Benchmarks suite alone and homology-clean sets that contain the three-class regulatory task: on the seven homology-clean tasks discriminability wins (0.039 vs 0.123) only through that task (0.040 vs 0.034 without it). Within clusters neither is resolvable. Real tasks therefore cannot isolate discriminability, which is why Route 1 rests on the synthetic dose-response; we now say so. Homology does not confound the relation (partial rho +0.74), but the audit found two errors on our side. Our 'homology-clean' subset still held two leaky tasks; dropping both gives rho = +1.00 (n=7, exact p=0.0004; +0.93, n=8, exact p=0.0022, if nt_enhancers_types is kept). And the 11 tasks are not independent units: they are 9 exact-duplicate-free sequence sets (nt_promoter_all is the union of the two other NT promoter tasks, nt_enhancers_types relabels nt_enhancers, and the regulatory task's OCR class is human_ocr_ensembl's positive class), and the promoter tasks of both suites share most promoter loci (73% of human_nontata_promoters' promoters lie mostly within nt_promoter_all's). With exact duplicates collapsed discriminability's rho stays +0.79 to +0.82 (exact p<=0.028); on the largest task sets sharing no loci (n=7) it is +0.71 to +0.82 (exact p 0.034-0.088), against +0.93 for GC content.

% (5) Limitations (i): sentence to add after the R^2 = +0.44 [-0.27, +0.70] sentence
A pre-registered multivariate analysis (nine covariates including length, within-class GC SD and train/test homology; nested leave-one-task-out) finds no covariate set that improves on discriminability (MAE 0.143 vs.\ 0.140, $\Delta$ CI $[-0.05,+0.07]$); test-set noise explains 1.5\% of the misfit, and the remaining heterogeneity is, post hoc, the split between the solved promoter and the failing enhancer/OCR tasks, which GC content tracks at least as closely as discriminability ($\rho{=}+0.86$ vs.\ $+0.74$).

% (6) Table II footnote (task non-independence; multivar_posthoc_task_identity.csv, _task_locus_links.csv)
The 11 tasks are 9 exact-duplicate-free sequence sets: \texttt{nt\_promoter\_all} is the union of the TATA and no-TATA tasks, \texttt{nt\_enhancers\_types} relabels \texttt{nt\_enhancers}, and the regulatory task's OCR class equals \texttt{human\_ocr\_ensembl}'s positives; beyond exact copies, the promoter tasks of both suites and the regulatory task share most promoter loci (31-mer containment; `no shared loci': largest sets with link $<$0.25); the $n{=}7$ row has $p{=}0.0028$ on its 6 exact-duplicate-free sets. Rows are sensitivity readouts of one correlation, not separate tests; $p$: exact permutation.

% (7) replacement for the Sec. Route 1 'Real-task corroboration' paragraph (120 words)
\textbf{Real-task consistency.} On the 11 TF-motif tasks discriminability tracks learnability (Spearman $\rho{=}+0.74$, $p{=}0.013$; leave-one-task-out MAE 0.14 MCC, 95\% CI $[0.11, 0.18]$), but GC content tracks it at least as closely ($\rho{=}+0.86$): the two are collinear ($\rho{=}+0.69$) and both separate the solved promoter from the failing enhancer/OCR tasks. Dropping the four tasks with $\ge$5\% train/test near-duplicates gives $\rho{=}+1.00$ ($n{=}7$; exact $p{=}0.0028$ on its 6 exact-duplicate-free sets; Table~\ref{tab:corr}), but the tasks are not independent: they are 9 exact-duplicate-free sequence sets, the promoter tasks share most promoter loci across suites, and on the largest sets sharing no loci ($n{=}7$) $\rho$ is $+0.71$ to $+0.82$ (GC: $+0.93$). The real-task relation is therefore consistent with the synthetic dose-response but is not independent evidence for it.
